title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment. A system built to support policing work was used by an officer to locate a private individual, and the searches were allegedly run repeatedly across more than one database rather than once. The misuse happened at the point of query, by an authorised user, which is the hardest place to catch: the system performed as designed and returned the information it was asked for.

Catching it would have required auditing who searched for whom and why, and treating repeated queries about one person as a signal rather than routine traffic. The facts do not establish what logging or review existed, whether any alert fired, or whether the searches were tied to any case. Nothing in the reporting shows the systems blocked or questioned the queries.

The accusation is that the officer used the tools to track a former partner, and it remains an accusation. A criminal complaint is not a conviction, the internal affairs outcome is not described, and the employment question is still before the town. The reporting does not establish intent, and no finding has been made.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She said he also used other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, and drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 for possible state law violations. After a four-week internal affairs investigation, the department placed him on paid leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has a restraining order against him for at least a year. The police chief said a Select Board hearing is scheduled next week, when town leaders could vote on Rogers' employment status.
